4802.html:
4802 *citth 'pound, tear'.
    S. cithaṇu 'to pound, bruise, hash'; L. citthaṇ 'to chew', (Ju.) cithaṇ; P. citthṇā 'to pound, crush, chew'; H. cīthnā 'to crush, tear'; M. cithṇẽ 'to take offence'. — Ext. with -ḍ-: S. cīthaṛo m. 'old ragged clothes', cithiṛaṇu, cithāṛ°, cethāṛ° 'to bruise, crush'; P. cīthṛā m. 'rag', Ku. cithṛo, N. cithro, cithornu 'to scratch, claw, get scratched'; H. cīthaṛ, °thṛā m. 'rag', cithāṛnā 'to tear to pieces'; G. cithṛũ n. 'rag'; — with -r-: G. cithrũ n., °rī f. 'rag'.

8138.html:
8138 pāṣāṇá 'stone' ṢaḍvBr. 2. pāṣāṇī- f. 'small stone used as a weight' lex. [Cf. pāṣī-. Early occurrence of -h- in Pk. and thence in NIA. (though in S. P. Si. -ṣ- regularly > -h-) is unexplained. Poss. connexion with *pāhāḍa-]
    1. Pa. pāsāṇa-, °aka- m. 'stone, rock', Pk. pāsāṇa-, pāhā̆ṇa- m.; S. pahaṇu m. 'stone', °ṇī f. 'pebble'; P. pāhaṇ m. 'stone', Mth. pāhan, OAw. pāhana m., H. pāhā̆n m., OG. pāhaṇiiṁ inst. sg. m., G. pāṇ, pahāṇɔ, pāṇɔ m., Si. pahaṇa, pāṇa. — X śāna-.
    2. B. pāṣāṇ 'the excess of weight in one scale which disturbs the equipoise'.
    Addenda: pāṣāṇá-: S.kcch. pāyaṇ, pāyṇo, pāṇo m. 'stone'.

12760.html:
12760 śvás² 'on the following day, tomorrow'. 2. śuvás (metr.) RV.
    1. Pa. svē, sē 'tomorrow', Si. seṭa, he° (adv. suffix -ṭa).
    2. Pa. suvē 'tomorrow'; Aś.top. suve suve 'day by day'; Pk. suvō, suvē 'tomorrow'; Dm. ċū 'yesternight'; WPah.pāḍ. śūī 'tomorrow'. — With unexpl. additions: Ash. šákeĩ 'tomorrow'; Kho. (Lor.) šupīṅga 'day after tomorrow'.
    aparaśvas, *ātriśvas, paraśvas.
